shared_elements: T-shaped monolithic pillar form (broad head over narrower shaft)
quadruped animal shown on the broad face of the shaft
animal rendered in relief clinging to / descending the vertical surface
faint incised lines on the lower shaft
justification: Both surfaces are the broad face of a T-headed pillar carrying an animal in relief, and in each case a quadruped is set on the shaft as if clinging to or descending the vertical plane, which is a fairly specific shared convention. The decisive difference is density and content: A carries a whole programme of registers (a row of quadrupeds beneath the head, a band of zigzag/net pattern, birds, a small human-like figure, a plant motif and long-necked birds low down), whereas B shows only a single small animal on an otherwise blank shaft, so almost all of A's iconography has no counterpart.
